Bra Cup Size Guide: From AA to K Letters and Volume Physics

Demystifying bra cup letters. Learn why cup size is relative to band size, how US and UK cup progressions differ, and how to find your true cup depth.

The Biggest Myth: Cup Size Has an Absolute Volume

Many people believe that an "A cup" is always small, a "C cup" is average, and a "D cup" is large. In truth, cup volume is completely relative to the band size.

Consider the volume of liquid that fills a bra cup:

  • 30D: Holds approximately 480 cc of tissue (Sister to 32C, 34B, 36A).
  • 34D: Holds approximately 710 cc of tissue (Sister to 36C, 38B, 40A).
  • 38D: Holds approximately 1000 cc of tissue.

A 38A cup actually holds more volume than a 30D cup!

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear, anatomically sound answers vetted by professional bra fitters.

Is a D cup always huge? ▾

No! A 'D cup' has no standalone volume. A 28D has the exact same cup volume as a 30C, 32B, and 34A—it holds roughly 390 cubic centimeters of breast tissue. On a slender frame, a 28D appears small to average. Cup letters only denote the difference between bust and ribcage.

Why do UK brands use double letters like FF and GG? ▾

UK lingerie manufacturers developed standardized 1-inch cup steps where double letters represent specific half-inch nuances or consecutive steps without skipping letters. Most professional fitters consider UK sizing the gold standard for D+ busts.
